newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota says no comment on possible Indian venture.
newsitem.headline: Toyota says no comment on possible Indian venture.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp on Monday declined comment on an Indian media report that the company would invest $240 million in a joint venture with India's Kirloskar group.
The Press Trust of India said on Sunday that Toyota would invest nearly $240 million of a total of $340 million in a joint venture to manufacture light commercial vehicles with the Kirloskar group.
"We cannot comment about the report. We are still in talks with the Kirloskar group over finalising details (of the possible venture)," a Toyota spokesman said.

The news agency quoted Vikram Kirloskar, a leading executive of the Kirloskar group, as saying that Toyota will hold 70 percent and the Indian group 30 percent in the project to be funded entirely by equity capital.
On Friday, Toyota executive vice-president Akira Yokoi told Reuters in Tokyo the company hoped to announce a joint venture before starting its summer holidays in Japan on August 9.
Yokoi said Bangalore was one of four possible sites for the venture. PTI said Bangalore was the likely choice.
In February, a Kirloskar official said Toyota would hold a stake of more than 50 percent in the proposed project, in which the Japanese firm would invest between 30 billion yen and 50 billion yen.
